# SPONTANEOUS BACTERIAL PERITONITIS (SBP)

[Oral step-down treatment](step-down-treatment)

SBP is infection of the peritoneal cavity in the absence of apparent trauma or other obvious cause. SBP occurs primarily in people with end-stage liver disease and ascites. The diagnosis is made when a peritoneal fluid sample has >/= 250 polymorphonuclear leukocyte cells per microliter, or when bacterial pathogens are isolated.

Long-term SBP prophylaxis is indicated for patients who experience a first episode of SBP.

## Prophylaxis for hospitalized patients with refractory low-protein ascites (less than 1 gm/dL peritoneal fluid)

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

Solomkin et al, Clin Infect Dis, 2010, 50:133-64
Up-to-Date article: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in adults: Treatment and prophylaxis
Therapy:
## Inpatient

Preferred:
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h for 5 days [M]

Alternative:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h for 5 days [R,DI]

## Prophylaxis in a patient with a previous SBP episode

Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q24h [R,DI]
< OR >
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q24h [R,DI]

## Prophylaxis in a patient with cirrhosis and variceal hemorrhage

Treat initially with an intravenous antimicrobial then step down to an oral antimicrobial when the patient can tolerate oral treatment.

Duration of therapy: Treat for a total of 7 days (intravenous and oral)

Preferred:
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h [M]

Alternative:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h [R,DI]

## Prophylaxis for hospitalized patients with refractory low-protein ascites

## (less than 1 gm/dL peritoneal fluid)

Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q24h until discharge from
hospital [R,DI]
< OR >
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q24h until discharge from hospital [R,DI]

## Outpatient

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

## Prophylaxis in a patient with a previous SBP episode

## ER

Treat initially with an intravenous antimicrobial then step down to an oral antimicrobial when the patient can tolerate oral treatment.

Duration of therapy: Treat for a total of 7 days (intravenous and oral)

Preferred:
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV once STAT [M]

Alternative:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Levofloxacin 750 mg IV once STAT [R,DI]
Inpt: ORZID2 GMENU ABX SPON BACT PERITONITIS
ERUC: ORZID GMENU ER/UC SPON BACT PERITONITIS
Outpt: ORZID3 GMENU ACUTE SPON BACT PERITONITIS
